schedule.vaccine: FeLV series if outdoor / multi-cat risk

bodySections.heading: Why timing matters
paragraphs: This outdoor cat plan sequences doses against felv/fiv exposure, not against a vague “sometime this season” intention for your cat.

Milestone labels on the outdoor cat table (8 weeks; 16 weeks; 16 weeks; Per clinic protocol) are operational deadlines for daycare, boarding, travel, and multi-pet intros — a nearly finished outdoor cat kitten series is still incomplete.

If your household also wrestles with fight wound risk or missed boosters during roaming season, put those constraints on the same calendar thread as the FeLV booster so one reminder system owns the outdoor cat week.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: Call the clinic with product names and prior dates the day you notice a missed outdoor cat dose; catch-up timing depends on age and gap length for this cat scenario.
Until the outdoor cat series is current again, reduce the exposure pattern that matches felv/fiv exposure, and do not wait for an annual wellness slot to ask about a outdoor cat make-up dose.
After the visit, enable 7-, 3-, and 1-day nudges for the next FeLV booster due date so the same outdoor cat miss cannot hide inside a shared family calendar.

faqs.question: Is this outdoor cat vaccine schedule a prescription?
faqs.answer: No. It is an editorial planning table aligned with common AAHA/AAFP-style windows and facility patterns. Your veterinarian sets the legal and medical plan for the individual cat.

faqs.question: What if we already missed a date on this outdoor cat schedule?
faqs.answer: Contact the clinic for catch-up timing. Bring prior records, limit high-risk exposure tied to felv/fiv exposure, and reset reminders as soon as the next outdoor cat due date is known.

faqs.question: How do reminders help with FeLV booster?
faqs.answer: PetClues can nudge you 7, 3, and 1 day before that outdoor cat booster is due so boarding and travel deadlines stop arriving as surprises.
